title: Choose the DOM X-Ray composition
question: Which first viewport should become the interactive result viewer? Choose one, or use the note to say what should carry across.

options.label: Instrument Panorama
options.thesis: A broad instrument rail, physical cutaway, and external machine make the entire measured system visible in one sweep.
options.viewport: The result model owns the center, URL and hero evidence sit at left, and the teal external-origin machine closes the right edge.
options.risk: The machinery and evidence field compete slightly with the page itself on a small laptop.

options.label: Exploded Evidence Poster
options.lineage: architectural section table, pushed toward feed impact
options.thesis: A diagonal exploded cutaway gives the result an unmistakable silhouette while one exact image becomes the red evidence moment.
options.viewport: The left action and 87.5% image fact stay quiet and huge; six layers sweep diagonally into one external-origin mechanism.
options.risk: The perspective must never imply that visual angle changes the measured geometry or ranking.

options.label: Measured Front Elevation
options.lineage: architectural section table, optimized for comprehension
options.thesis: A nearly front-on plate stack makes DOM depth, the hero fact, and the evidence drawer legible before any interaction.
options.viewport: A measured central elevation carries the 4-of-8 external-domain fact; one teal origin machine and one evidence drawer occupy the right.
options.risk: Its calm symmetry is clearest, but the static poster has less immediate motion energy than the diagonal option.
